A Tribute to
Mrs. Simone Tata
Chairperson Emeritus
2nd March 1930 – 5th December 2025We honour and celebrate the remarkable life and legacy of  
Mrs. Simone Tata, Chairperson Emeritus of Trent, whose vision 
and leadership have left an enduring mark on the organisation.
Mrs. Tata’s exceptional understanding of fashion, style, and consumer behaviour 
reshaped the retail experience in India. With the opening of the first Westside 
store in Bengaluru, she brought to life a thoughtful vision of creating a brand that 
offered refined and meaningful lifestyle choices to Indian households. Her clarity 
of purpose and commitment to excellence continue to shape Trent’s approach to 
quality, design, and customer experience.
Beyond her professional accomplishments, Mrs. Tata was deeply committed to 
making a difference in society. Her contributions to philanthropic initiatives, 
particularly in supporting women and children, reflect her compassion and sense 
of responsibility.
Mrs. Tata’s legacy lives on through the values she championed and the 
strong foundation she built. Her vision continues to inspire and guide 
Trent as it carries forward the foundation she so thoughtfully built.
We remember and celebrate her with deep respect and gratitude.Mrs. TataIt’s all so new, they kept saying.
It is the future, I kept insisting.

Reporting Approach
This Report presents a 
comprehensive and integrated overview of Trent Limited’s (‘the Company’ or ‘Trent’) performance and value creation journey. It brings together financial and non-financial information to provide stakeholders with meaningful insights into the Company’s business strategy, operating environment, governance framework, key priorities, risk landscape, sustainability initiatives, as well as its approach to creating long-term value for all its stakeholders.
Framewo rks, Guidelines 
and Stan dards
This Report is guided by the principles of the International Integrated Reporting Council (IIRC) Framework. The statutory reports, including the 
Board’s Report
Management Discussion & Analysis (MD&A)
Corporate Governance Report
Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report (BRSR)
Standalone and Consolidated Financial Statements,  are in line with the applicable Indian Accounting Standards, the Companies Act, 2013, Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, and the Secretarial Standards issued by the Institute of Company Secretaries of India.Forward-Looking 
Statements
This Report contains certain forward-
looking statements concerning our business operations, financial position, strategy, objectives, and future performance. These statements are based on current assumptions and expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and evolving business conditions. While we believe the assumptions are reasonable, actual outcomes may differ materially. The Company undertakes no obligation to publicly update forward-looking statements, whether as a result of new information, future events, or otherwise, except as required by the applicable laws and regulations.
Feedback
We value stakeholder engagement and welcome your feedback on our performance and reporting. For queries or suggestions, please contact:BDO India Services Private Limited has provided reasonable assurance on the non-financial disclosures included in BRSR Report (BRSR Core) for the reporting period, in accordance with the International Standards on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) and International Standards on Assurance Engagements 3410 standards, issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards  Board (IAASB).
Scope and Reporting 
Bound ary
This Report covers the standalone and consolidated financial performance of Trent, including its subsidiaries, associate and group companies, for the financial year from 1
st April 2025 to 31st March 2026. The 
standalone and consolidated financial statements have been audited by Deloitte Haskins & Sells LLP, Chartered Accountants. Non-financial information has been reported primarily on a standalone basis for Trent. Given the materiality and future growth agenda, select coverage of our food business under the Star banner has also been included.

=== page 8 ===
As I look back at Trent’s journey, I am filled with a deep 
sense of reflection. What started as a thoughtful transition 
from Lakmé into an emerging fashion retail space has, over time, become something ever more meaningful. 
On a personal note, I often reflect on the early conversations 
I had with my mother, Mrs. Simone Tata, when we were considering the transition of Lakmé into a new direction. At the heart of those discussions was a simple but powerful aspiration - to create products and experiences that people truly love and desire and yet rooted in Tata values. It is deeply satisfying to see that, in many ways, this aspiration has come to fruition through Trent’s progress over the past two and a half decades.
In 1998, when we began with a single Westside store at 
Commercial Street in Bengaluru, modern fashion retail in India was almost non-existent. The idea of creating a contemporary, accessible retail experience for Indian consumers was both ambitious and uncertain. Yet, it was also energising - because we were not just building a business, we were participating in shaping a new business category in the country.
More than 25 years later, the transformation has been 
extraordinary - first and foremost for India itself.  The India we operate in today is vastly different. There is a greater exposure to global trends, rising aspirations across demographics, and an increasing ability among consumers to pursue lifestyle choices. The growth in disposable incomes and the desire for self-expression through fashion have fundamentally reshaped consumption patterns.
We have witnessed a remarkable evolution - not only in 
people’s sense of fashion, but also in how they think, choose, and live. The proliferation of choice, the openness to change, and the confidence of the Indian consumer  have all contributed to creating a vibrant and  competitive marketplace.
Through all these changes, I am extremely proud that Trent 
has remained grounded and anchored firmly in the values of the Tata group. Even as the environment became more Dear Shareholders,
dynamic and competitive, and even as consumer expectations underwent dramatic shifts, our focus on delivering genuine customer value has remained unwavering.
From a single Westside store to a network of over twelve 
hundred stores, our journey has been one of steady evolution. Over the years, we have added powerful growth engines to our portfolio - most notably Zudio and Star - which are now a significant part of our portfolio. The strength of Trent today lies not just in scale, but in the diversity and relevance of our brands.We have also worked towards building an integrated ecosystem - across design, sourcing, supply chain, and retail execution - to ensure that each of our brands delivers a differentiated and compelling customer experience. This ability to combine back-end strength with front-end innovation has been central to our progress.
I have long believed that Trent is not intended to be defined 
by a single brand, but rather by a portfolio of brands. In a diverse and evolving market like India as well as globally, it is unlikely that any one brand can capture a dominant share of the lifestyle space. Instead, our approach has been to create distinct, well-defined propositions that cater to different customer needs and occasions. This multi-brand strategy will continue to guide our future.
As we look ahead, I firmly believe that the best years of 
Trent are ahead of us. The opportunities before us are vast -  
not just in India. In the years to come, I see Trent touching even more lives through our offerings, expanding across categories, and exploring new geographies  over time.
It would be enormously satisfying to shape and build 
brands from India that go on to be globally relevant in diverse markets. Further, as we consider this future, we should also aspire for material scale of revenues from overseas markets. This would be completely in line with the national agenda of growing value added exports from our country. We should aspire boldly, execute with perseverance and celebrate the pride of brands - built ground up from India!
As we move forward, our journey will remain deeply 
collaborative. Our stakeholders - our employees, partners, suppliers, communities, and shareholders - are integral to everything we do. Together, we will continue to build a responsible, sustainable, and meaningful business of scale.
Given the significant opportunities that remain ahead and 
the growing strength of Trent’s platform, I believe we are still at an early phase of our growth journey.  With a strong ecosystem around us and a clear sense of purpose, we are positioned to build upon this platform.In our 2023 shareholders meeting, I had envisioned Trent to be ten times bigger in terms of revenues with commensurate profitability. Since then, the revenue and profitability run rate has grown by over 2.5 times. Given all this, I am confident that we will reach the milestone I had referenced in the not-so-distant future.
I sincerely thank you for your continued trust in Trent and for 
being an integral part of our journey.
NOEL N. TATA
Chairman
Message from the Chairman

Letter from the Managing Director
FY26 marked another year of meaningful progress for Trent, 
driven by a portfolio anchored in customer relevance, strong 
value propositions, and long-term engagement. Our core fashion brands - Westside and Zudio - continued to deliver strong, complementary growth across segments. We are also encouraged by the early momentum with Burnt Toast, our new lifestyle brand proposition that appeals to trend-forward and Gen-Z consumers.
Our food and grocery business, Star continues to evolve in a 
significant way, building on the Trent playbook. The year saw substantial interventions with respect to the operating model with a refreshed emphasis on in-store customer experience. We remain encouraged by the traction that our own brand propositions are witnessing across micro markets. Own brands now contribute to 73% of Star’s revenues and remain the core differentiating proposition of the brand.  
We continue to pursue a disciplined expansion program that 
is aimed at growing share of presence in existing micro markets as well as establishing reach to numerous new cities and towns across India. This growth has been supported by a more robust operating backbone, enabling quicker turnarounds, faster refresh cycles, and improved execution  
at scale.
Alongside footprint expansion, we maintained a strong focus 
on financial discipline - optimising store-level margins and leveraging digital platforms to strengthen our omni-channel connect. Our teams remain central to execution in a relatively challenging macroeconomic context, driving productivity improvements across multiple areas and reinforcing a culture  
of pursuing excellence.
Technology and digital initiatives remained key enablers for 
Trent during the year. We continued to strengthen our digital ecosystem by investing in the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), data analytics, and automation to enhance product design, merchandise planning, improve supply chain efficiency, and elevate in-store and omni-channel customer experiences. AI-led use cases are increasingly supporting demand forecasting, inventory optimisation, and delivery of a more customer-relevant engagement across channels. Dear Shareholders,
As we look ahead, we do so with confidence and an unwavering commitment to serve our customers better every day. To our colleagues, partners, and shareholders - thank  
you for your trust and support. We remain energised by the opportunity ahead and are determined to build a future-ready Trent that creates enduring value.
P. VENKATESALU
Managing Director

Delivering Diﬀerentiated Retail Experiences
Trent is one of the 
leading players in the branded lifestyle space in India. Our diﬀerentiated brands, that bring quality, aﬀordability, and an enhanced customer experience, enable us to cater to a diverse and evolving consumer base across markets.Our key fashion brand concepts - Westside, Zudio, Samoh, and Burnt Toast -  
are each defined by a distinct identity and a clear consumer proposition. In 
the food and grocery segment, we operate under the Star banner, supported by a cohesive and scalable business architecture.

Governance that Reinforces Trust
Board Composition
The Board consists of seven 
Directors, of whom four are Independent Directors, representing 57.1% of its composition (including 2 women directors constituting 28.6%). The remaining members include two Non-Executive, Non-Independent Directors, including the Chairman, besides the Managing Director.We lead with integrity, 
accountability, and transparency as core values rooted in the Tata ethos. This shapes how we manage risk, allocate capital, and engage  with stakeholders to create consistent, long-term value.Governance Structure
Our governance framework is 
designed to promote accountability and informed decision-making across the organisation. It is guided by the Tata Code of Conduct and our internal policies. All employees are expected to follow Trent’s values and act with honesty, fairness, and integrity.  
We follow a structured and inclusive 
approach to decision-making to ensure consistency and transparency. All decisions are aligned with the Company’s overall objectives and long-term strategy, supporting sustainable growth. This approach also strengthens governance practices and enhances overall organisational effectiveness. 
The structure operates through 
multiple tiers: the Board of Directors, Board Committees, the Managing Director and the Leadership Team. The Board brings together members with extensive business experience and strong credibility across sectors. Their diverse expertise and independent perspectives strengthen deliberations. The Board acts in good faith, with due diligence, care and in the best interests of the shareholders.
Board Committees form an integral 
part of this framework. They are delegated specific responsibilities by the Board. These Committees  provide focused oversight and guidance across key areas such as audit, risk management, nomination and remuneration, stakeholder relations, governance, CSR, and sustainability, enhancing the Board’s ability to discharge its responsibilities thoroughly and efficiently.
The Managing Director and the 
Leadership Team lead strategy and drive execution, ensuring operational excellence and sustained growth.

Board Familiarisation
The Board receives periodic updates on the Tata Code of Conduct, relevant regulatory changes, and developments in areas 
such as ethics and governance, health and safety, CSR and sustainability, insider trading, business performance, strategy, and compliance matters. These updates enable informed oversight and decision-making.Board Responsibilities
The Board understands the business dynamics and environment under which the Company operates, challenges and opportunities associated with the business operations and provides guidance, oversight, and strategic direction to the management. The Board always acts in good faith, with due diligence, care, and in the best interests of the shareholders.

Industry Dynamics and Market Environment
India remains one of the 
fastest-growing major economies, supported by strong macroeconomic fundamentals and ongoing reforms. Rising incomes, urbanization, and evolving consumer preferences continue to drive consumption-led growth, creating signiﬁcant opportunities for the retail sector. India is poised to become the third-largest economy with USD 7.3 Trillion GDP by 2030
1, reﬂecting 
its expanding role  and inﬂuence in the  global economy.Rising Middle Class 
and Aspirational Consumption
A rapidly expanding middle-income 
population, supported by rising earning capacity, is driving discretionary spending across lifestyle categories such as fashion, accessories, and consumer goods. As purchasing power strengthens, consumers increasingly move beyond basic purchases toward branded and value-driven offerings, supporting growth in organised  retail formats.
Growing Demand from 
Tier II and Tier III Markets
Consumption growth in emerging 
cities is becoming a key driver of retail expansion. Rising aspirations and improving local incomes are increasing acceptance of branded merchandise, enabling organised retailers to deepen market penetration beyond metropolitan regions and widen access to quality products.
Urbanisation Supporting 
Modern Retail Expansion
Continued urban migration is 
transforming cities into consumption hubs, increasing demand for malls and integrated retail destinations. Shopping spaces are evolving into lifestyle centres that combine retail, entertainment, and dining, encouraging longer customer engagement and higher in-store spending.Strengthening 
Organised Retail
Regulatory reforms and the 
government push to drive economic growth have simplified compliance and improved supply chain efficiency, enabling greater transparency and faster inventory movement. Alongside this, policy reforms such as easier approvals, improved ease of doing business, and supportive investment policies are strengthening retail infrastructure. The expansion of logistics networks, warehouses, and commercial spaces is helping organised retailers scale efficiently and enter underserved markets.
Digital Acceleration and 
Phygital Retail
Technology adoption is reshaping 
consumer journeys by integrating online discovery with offline fulfilment. Digital platforms and personalised engagement tools improve convenience and conversion, while phygital retail models combine e-commerce reach with the trust of physical stores through unified experiences and flexible fulfilment options.Advancements in 
Logistics and Fulﬁlment Capabilities
The emergence of micro-fulfilment 
centres, modern warehousing, and just-in-time inventory systems are enhancing supply chain agility. These advancements enable faster replenishment, improved availability, and cost efficiencies, allowing retailers to respond effectively to dynamic consumer demand.
Preference for 
Experience-Led and Value Fashion Retail
Modern shoppers increasingly 
seek engaging environments that blend convenience with inspiration. Experience-focused destinations and value fashion offerings that balance quality, design, and affordability are gaining strong traction among price-conscious yet brand-aware consumers.

Risk Management
Risk Governance
The Risk Management Committee, the Audit Committee, and the Board review 
periodic updates on key enterprise risks and material changes in the Company’s risk profile, ensuring effective oversight at the highest levels. The execution of the risk management framework is driven by a central Risk Management function under the leadership of the Chief Financial Officer, enabling a consistent and coordinated approach across the organisation. The Company has adopted the COSO 2017 Enterprise Risk Management Framework for driving its risk management agenda. Ongoing communication initiatives and structured risk workshops promote awareness, accountability, and transparency in risk reporting. The use of technology and advanced analytics supports efficient, accurate, and timely monitoring of risks.Our structured 
Enterprise Risk Management framework, aligned with the COSO 2017 framework, provides eﬀective oversight across governance, strategy, and business operations. This integrated approach embeds risk considerations into strategic and operational decisions, reinforcing resilience, protecting value, and promoting a culture of disciplined decision-making.Risk Management Process
Assess Risk Response
Regular reviews and structured 
discussions enable risk owners and management to reassess exposure levels, evaluate the effectiveness of mitigation plans and undertake corrective actions.Develop Risk Response
Mitigation strategies are structured around defined risk appetite and tolerance thresholds, with actions calibrated through risk acceptance, reduction, sharing or transfer,  as appropriate.
Monitor, Communicate and Report
The management and leadership team engages on a regular basis to review the Company’s risk profile and evaluate the effectiveness of the risk management framework.Identify and Analyse
Risks are systematically identified and assessed across each  business and support function along  
with an enterprise-wide, top-down perspective provided by the Board, the Audit Committee, and the Risk Management Committee.Assess and Prioritise
Each identified risk is evaluated across impact, likelihood, and velocity, with due consideration to strategic priorities and  operational deliverables. Key Market Risks and Mitigation Plan
 Geopolitical risks, such as wars, conflicts, and sanctions, can disrupt trade, investment, and financial stability, leading to economic downturns and fluctuations in asset prices. Conversely, macroeconomic risks encompass broader economic factors that can affect the economy’s performance, such as inflation, interest rates, and economic growth. We continuously monitor and reduce reliance on volatile trade routes and proactively prepare for regional disruptions.
 Maintaining liquidity buffers ensures minimal disruption and stable operations.
 Navigating through regional restrictions and adapting through quick and effective responses has helped us build long-term resilience and deliver sustained growth.Macro 
Environmental Risk
 Trend relevance is central to our 
business. Any inability to anticipate or respond swiftly to evolving fashion preferences and changing consumer expectations poses a direct risk.
 Intensifying competition, the growing attractiveness of the sector and rapid technological innovation further heighten market complexity.
 At the same time, curating retail spaces, assortments and displays across diverse micro-markets and demographic segments adds executional challenges. Misalignment on these dimensions can materially impact consumer outcomes and delivered margins. Continuous monitoring of the market and competitive landscape, combined with active customer engagement, enables early identification of evolving needs and changes in the fashion trends.
 Ongoing efforts to spot emerging fashion trends are reinforced by strong in-house design capabilities, supported by design studios in India and Spain, ensuring a refreshed and relevant product portfolio.
 Systematic identification and incubation of growth drivers and enablers support sustained business performance.
 Space management algorithms are calibrated to reflect regional and local variations, enhancing relevance and productivity across markets.
 A disciplined focus on margins, cost efficiency, quality, and compliance underpins a sustainable operating model aligned with changing consumer expectations.Industry

Resiliency for Trent is all about being 
relevant over time to a growing critical mass of customers in the lifestyle space. It is about the relative desirability of respective brand propositions in an otherwise crowded and competitive market place.
At the next level, resilience should 
translate to relatively consistent performance across cycles notwithstanding a rapidly evolving consumer and competitive context. Performance outcomes should encompass growing revenues and customer base, strong unit economics, overall profitability and capital efficiencies. Also, a resilient business should importantly afford the trial, incubation and build out of additional growth engines (brands/ categories/ geographies) over time.
How are we managing this:
Own brands
Our business model choices are at the core of delivering desirable customer propositions. The emphasis is on our own brands and nimble responsiveness to emerging consumer preferences. The pursuit with each of our brands is for distinctive market positioning that is differentiated. Strong product disciplines including ownership of product design and curation, focus on speed of concept to market and consistency of offer across channels, are a defining feature of  our playbook.
Direct to consumer
Trent is quintessentially direct-to-consumer as we adopt direct distribution and eschew third-party channels and intermediation of any kind. We focus on being accessible with the ubiquitous presence of our Trent’s digital advantage comes from what it owns and operates - its supply chain, brands, and distribution network of over 1,250 stores. Together, these generate proprietary, first-hand data across the value chain, from product creation and movement to customer response. This data forms the foundation of the Company’s AI and analytics capability.
The Company’s approach is 
business-led and designed around reinforcing intelligence loops, not isolated point solutions. Insights from trendspotting, demand sensing, buying, merchandising, supply chain, and customer engagement feed into one another, helping the business make faster, sharper, and more informed decisions.
This capability was initially built 
through a central Centre of Excellence to create foundational tools, standards and reusable models. It is now being embedded deeper into the business, with data science teams working alongside designers, buyers, merchandisers and supply chain teams. This integration helps translate AI from prototypes into repeatable sources of advantage.
Trent sees this work less as artificial 
intelligence and more as intelligence amplification. The aim is to enhance human judgement, instinct and expertise — not replace them. Technology extends the reach of people; the intelligence remains human, while the leverage becomes machine and the underlying AI models and tools.
During the year, the Company 
advanced AI-led interventions aligned to its strategic priorities of strengthening brands, deepening stores (and online in the case of Westside) and building a critical mass of presence in micro markets to drive awareness. This model facilitates a strong organic connection with our customers while at the same time affording better economics.
Control over the value chain
Our playbook involves complete ownership/ control over multiple parts of our value chain, from sourcing and production facilities to retailing. We believe many of these choices and disciplines (and in many respects counterintuitive at first instance) are integral to realising strong differentiation, agility, and relevance  of the brands over time.
Integrated back and 
diﬀerentiated front
Trent has evolved into a platform with 
multiple retail brand propositions and the intent is to operate with a portfolio of growth engines (retail brands/ categories/ geographies). We adopt a deeply differentiated approach to the customer-facing aspects of brands, and at the same time, a deeply integrated approach with respect  to systems, processes,  and infrastructure.
Technology and supply chain 
investments
Given the scale and the rapidly 
evolving consumer context, we are committing substantial investments in technology, automation, and the supply chain. For instance, across the fashion portfolio, we have transitioned to universal RFID tagging and tracking of merchandise. We are increasingly leveraging multiple technology and AI interventions and starting to witness material outcomes.Structural cost management  
Structural cost management coupled with a focus on operating efficiencies is integral to our strategic priority of building resilience, particularly as we continue to scale in a dynamic operating environment. Our focus is on building an operating model that remains agile, disciplined, and adaptable across cycles.  We undertake several interventions across process transformation, standardisation and productivity, workforce planning and store design. For instance, RFID adoption across the supply chain and store operations has enabled a significant reduction in several time-intensive activities. These continuing interventions are aimed at improving operating efficiencies and enhancing productivity at scale.
Organizational culture and 
capabilities
People capabilities and a distinctive 
organisational culture are integral to the delivery of outcomes we are pursuing. We adopt a yin & yang approach by both incorporating talent with a track record in select areas and at the same time prioritizing a growing pool of young talent. In a significant way, our ability to be resilient depends on continuing to solve puzzles with respect to capabilities, a strong discipline stack, and a culture that is collegial & agile.
Over time, we seek to build out a 
compelling and future-fit portfolio of lifestyle brands, each commanding a distinctive consumer image and addressing a substantial  market opportunity.customer understanding, improving availability, extending reach, and advancing sustainability. Trendspotting capabilities supported product strategy by identifying emerging consumer preferences. Personalised campaign engines enabled more relevant engagement during festive and sale periods. GIS and AI-led location intelligence strengthened store expansion decisions with greater objectivity, speed, and precision.
The Company also improved 
customer experience through automation in refund monitoring and support workflows, enabling faster response and resolution. A centralised insights platform was developed to bring enterprise-wide data into actionable intelligence for more agile decision-making.Trent approaches AI with clear governance, safety, and ethics. The Company does not deploy fully autonomous systems for consequential decisions; humans remain in the loop. Systems are designed as workflow agents that assist and accelerate human work, rather than act unsupervised.
Through initiatives such as its 
collaboration with NASSCOM on the AgentFlow Innovation Challenge, Trent continues to explore scalable, future-ready AI capabilities. Its AI journey remains focused on measurable business outcomes across revenue growth, operational efficiency, customer experience and  workforce productivity.

Sustainability - Strategy and Governance
Our sustainability 
journey is closely aligned with the Tata Group’s Project Aalingana, reﬂecting a shared purpose of building climate resilience and advancing responsible business practices. This commitment is further strengthened by globally recognised frameworks such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs) and the National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct (NGRBC), which guide us in creating long-term, inclusive value.Sustainability 
Governance
Our sustainability efforts are driven 
through well-defined governance and collaboration across teams. A dedicated internal team, drawing on cross-functional expertise, works collaboratively to translate our commitments into action across the organisation. This ensures that sustainability is not siloed but seamlessly integrated into  business operations.
At the leadership level, the CSR and 
Sustainability Committee, along with the Board, provides strategic direction and oversight, ensuring that our sustainability priorities remain closely aligned with our long-term vision for value creation. Complementing this, the Risk Management Committee plays a critical role in identifying and overseeing ESG-related risks, ensuring that robust mitigation strategies are in place. 
Together, these layers of governance 
create a structured and  forward-looking framework that  supports responsible growth  and accountability.At Trent, sustainability is not a standalone initiative - it is embedded into the way we think, operate, and grow. As we expand our footprint, we are equally mindful of the impact we create, ensuring that environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations shape our everyday business choices.

Be Resource Eﬃcient
Goals
 Replace the use of fossil fuel-based energy with 
renewable energy by 50% of intensity per sq. ft. and reduce consumption by 10% per sq. ft., by F Y27.
 Eliminate non-recyclable packaging materials across value chain, by FY28.Progress till Now
 We have installed Internet of Things (IoT) systems in 700+ stores, enabling a more uniform customer experience and helping us establish a consistent operational baseline. 
 The Company has adopted a focused approach towards energy transition, with emphasis on solar integration and improved energy utilisation. 
 Rooftop solar installations meet over one -third of 
electricity demand at three distribution centres. We have completed a baseline assessment of our energy  consumption and are actively progressing toward achieving our FY 2026-27 sustainability goals.
 About 70% of our plastic waste is traceable and processed, marking a key milestone in our journey toward 100% waste recycling by 2028. 
 We are also transitioning to durable, reusable totes in place of cardboard cartons for circular transit between distribution centres and stores.Goals and ProgressAt Trent, our approach to resource efficiency is shaped by a simple belief: responsible growth must go hand in hand with mindful use of natural resources. Materiality Assessment
Our materiality 
assessment enables prioritisation of ESG areas that drive stakeholder trust, resilience, and long-term value.  It is undertaken as a disciplined evaluation of issues most relevant  to the business and  its stakeholders.A Structured and Inclusive Process
At Trent, we undertook our materiality assessment engaging a diverse group of 
internal leaders and external stakeholders. This process enabled us to identify key sustainability priorities, which serve as important drivers in aligning our business objectives with stakeholder expectations. Our materiality approach is guided by the Indian regulatory framework (NGRBC) and the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) standards.
The Three-Step Framework
Identiﬁcation
We identified the ESG themes most relevant to our business context and operating landscape by:
 Analysing regulatory requirements (including  BRSR disclosures)
 Reviewing industry benchmarks and emerging ESG trends
 Assessing peer practices
 Evaluating issues material  to our operations and  stakeholder expectationsPrioritisation
Each identified topic was evaluated through a dual lens, to ensure focus on issues with the greatest strategic and reputational relevance:
 Its significance to stakeholders
 Its impact on business performance and long-term value creation
Materiality Mapping
Prioritised themes were mapped on a 3x3 materiality matrix, reflecting diverse stakeholder perspectives and business impact.
The matrix serves as a strategic compass guiding resource allocation, risk 
management and our sustainability roadmap.

Innovative Design for High-Quality Products
Creativity and product 
discipline form the foundation of how we develop oﬀerings that resonate with our customers. Our approach integrates the entire product value chain, from design and development to curation and in-store presentation, ensuring that concepts are translated eﬃciently into compelling products on the shelf while maintaining consistency across channels. In-House Design Driving 
Product Diﬀerentiation
At the core of this capability is a 
dedicated in-house creative team that designs and develops our entire portfolio across fashion, lifestyle, and home categories. By continuously researching global influences and analysing evolving market trends, our design teams bring fresh perspectives and distinctive products that keep our offerings relevant, differentiated, and aligned with contemporary  consumer aspirations.
Fashion-Led Design and 
Intelligent Creation
Our captive design studios serve as the 
creative engine behind the distinctive fashion identity of our brands. Our teams closely track global fashion movements and interpret them into contemporary designs that resonate with evolving consumer preferences. This creative capability is increasingly strengthened through the integration of AI and advanced analytics within the design process. 
Leveraging Generative AI, designers 
gain sharper insights into emerging colour palettes, silhouettes, patterns, and fabric directions, complemented by weekly trading intelligence and material analysis. The convergence of creative intuition and data-led foresight enables us to craft distinctive collections with agility, ensuring our offerings remain relevant, trend-aligned, and compelling in a dynamic fashion landscape. Product Safety and 
Customer Protection
We remain committed to responsible 
marketing practices and the maintenance of the highest standards of product integrity across our brands. Our products are designed and sourced in compliance with applicable safety and quality standards, supported by regular assessments that help identify and address potential gaps. We also prioritise the protection of customer information, ensuring strict data privacy and confidentiality through stringent security protocols.
Transparent Marketing 
and Consumer Awareness
Our marketing and product 
communications are guided by transparency and accountability. We ensure that product information, labelling, and promotional messages across touchpoints are clear, accurate, and aligned with established advertising standards. Customers are encouraged to share feedback or raise concerns regarding products or marketing communications, which are addressed through a structured grievance redressal process to ensure timely and responsible resolution.
Listening to Customers
Customer feedback is critical to us and we continuously monitor customer interactions across multiple channels. This helps us capture insights  at scale and respond quickly to  customer needs.Digital, Data and 
Analytics Centre of Excellence 
The Digital, Data and Analytics Centre 
of Excellence is focused on translating complex data into actionable business insights, strengthening the quality and speed of decision-making. By embedding predictive analytics into key processes, we are enabling our design and buying teams to anticipate demand shifts and respond with greater precision to evolving customer preferences. 
Enhancing Store Design 
and Customer Experience 
During the year, we undertook a 
design evolution in our Westside store façades by transitioning from blue glass to clear glass, with the objective of enhancing both functionality and customer experience. 
 This has introduced higher levels of natural light, creating brighter and more welcoming retail environments while enabling more flexible and disciplined store layouts.
 The transparent glass box structure enhances store visibility, creates a contemporary global aesthetic,  and elevates the overall  shopping experience.
 It also supports low power consumption, aligning with our sustainability goals.

Building a Resilient Supply Chain
Strong supplier 
partnerships are integral to Trent’s ability to operate eﬃciently and respond swiftly to evolving customer preferences. We work closely with our supplier partner network to ensure responsible sourcing, consistent quality, and that desirable products reach our customers in a timely manner. Supplier Evaluatio n and 
Responsible Sour cing
We prioritise responsible sourcing by 
working with supplier partners who align with our ethical, environmental, and operational standards. Supplier Partners’ evaluation play a key role in ensuring supply continuity, product quality, and long-term partnership value. Supplier partners are assessed on their ability to meet business requirements, while upholding our principles of responsible and transparent operations.
An efficient and resilient backend 
remains central to our ability to deliver fresh, relevant merchandise to stores with speed, discipline, and cost efficiency. Over time, we have built an integrated supply chain ecosystem that supports rapid expansion while maintaining high service standards and strong governance.
More than 90% of our product 
suppliers have undergone SEDEX SMETA 4-pillar audits, which evaluate performance across labour practices, health and safety, environmental management, and business ethics, including human rights considerations.
SEDEX SMETA 4-Pillars
Labour Standards
This pillar evaluates adherence to labour laws and ethical employment practices, including working hours, wages, child labour, forced labour, and freedom of association, ensuring fair treatment and safe working conditions for workers.
Health and Safety Standards
This pillar assesses workplace safety systems, preventive measures against accidents, and occupational illness, emergency preparedness, and initiatives that support the overall well-being of employees.Environmental Standards
This pillar reviews the environmental footprint of operations, focusing on responsible resource use, waste management, pollution control, and compliance with environmental regulations to promote  
sustainable practices.
Business Ethics
This pillar examines ethical business conduct, including anti-corruption policies, transparency, and fair commercial practices, ensuring accountability and integrity across business relationships.
Both new and existing supplier partners 
are periodically assessed against defined environmental and social criteria. These assessments help identify improvement opportunities and strengthen supplier partners’ capabilities through structured feedback, audit documentation, and continuous engagement with our teams.
Supplier Partners  
Capability Building
We actively collaborate with our supplier partners to strengthen operational efficiency, encourage responsible fabric sourcing, and improve social and environmental compliance. Our teams also support supplier partners in adopting technology-driven processes to monitor production and quality milestones. To reinforce consistent standards, we have implemented the Trent Vendor Code of Conduct, which guides supplier partners in maintaining responsible business practices.
We continue to invest in a future-ready 
supply chain through technology and  automation. RFID-enabled tracking across apparel and footwear enhances visibility, reduces discrepancies, and simplifies store operations. Accents, a digital Procure to Pay (P2P) portal, enables our supplier partners to engage and transact digitally with us, enhancing transparency and their satisfaction levels.Creating Impact

Infrastructure for Oncology Personnel Initiative
The Skilling and Supportive 
Infrastructure for Oncology Personnel initiative addresses the shortage of healthcare professionals in India, driven by uneven urban–rural distribution, limited training capacity, migration, and low public health investment. The challenge is more acute in Tier 2 cities such as Tirupati and Ranchi, where gaps in cancer care infrastructure and skilled manpower persist. The programme focusses on building dedicated infrastructure to train oncology personnel and provide residential support for nurses.
At the Sri Venkateswara Institute of 
Cancer Care & Research (SVICCAR), Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh, the initiative strengthens access to specialised cancer care while enabling the recruitment of nurses from across districts and states, improving both capacity and patient outcomes.

Conservation and Security Initiative
Chandrapur district in Maharashtra 
faces acute water stress due to groundwater over-extraction, and inadequate soil and water conservation infrastructure.
In partnership with Collectives for 
Integrated Livelihood Initiatives (CInI), the programme strengthens water security across vulnerable rural communities in the Mul and Pombhurna blocks. Guided by Village Water Security Plans, it adopts an integrated approach combining water conservation and harvesting interventions such as gabion structures, field bunding, desiltation of tanks, ponds and nalas, and the construction and restoration of check dams. Sustainable practices like drip irrigation and mulching further enhance water use efficiency and farm resilience.
The initiative improves irrigation 
access, enhances water storage, and builds long-term resilience of rural livelihoods. An evidence-based geohydrology approach underpins groundwater management, enabling sustainable and scalable impact.Essential Enablers

Advancing Environmental Sustainability
As we continue to expand 
our footprint, we remain committed to minimising environmental impact through responsible resource management. We actively explore ways to conserve natural resources while improving the eﬃciency of our energy use, emissions management, and waste reduction across operations. Creating Impact
Sustainability 
Pillars
Strategic Priorities
Capitals 
SDGsBe Resource Eﬃcient
Material Issues Sustainable Products and Services
GHG Emissions and Energy ConsumptionPackaging and WasteNatural Capital NBrand ResilienceEnergy Consumption and 
Emissions
As Trent continues to expand its retail 
footprint, energy plays a critical role in powering our day-to-day operations - from lighting and cooling our stores to supporting connected systems across offices and distribution centres.
Over the past year, our energy 
consumption and associated emissions have increased, reflecting the addition of new stores, the expansion of existing formats, and a higher scale of operations. While this growth is a natural outcome of business momentum, it also reinforces the importance of managing resources responsibly. Encouragingly, our energy intensity per product has remained stable, indicating that efficiency measures are helping balance the impact of scale. This reflects our ongoing efforts to optimise energy use even as volumes grow.
We have also completed a baseline 
assessment of our energy consumption, providing a clear foundation as we actively progress towards achieving our sustainability goals.
Driving Energy Eﬃciency
At Trent, improving energy efficiency is an ongoing priority as we continue to scale our operations. Our focus is on adopting technologies and upgrading infrastructure in ways that not only optimise energy use but also enhance the in-store experience for customers  and colleagues.
A key enabler in this journey has been 
the introduction of technology-led, data-driven solutions across our store network. We have deployed an IoT-enabled central monitoring and automation platform that brings greater intelligence and control to energy management at our operating locations.
The new system integrates smart energy meters, IoT-enabled thermostats, and intelligent sensors to track real-time power consumption, automate cooling and lighting based on occupancy, and monitor equipment health for timely maintenance. A centralised command dashboard now allows for continuous monitoring, benchmarking, and proactive intervention across  our stores.
Alongside these digital interventions, 
we continue to strengthen our physical infrastructure. This includes transitioning to LED lighting systems and deploying DX inverter-based air-conditioning, both of which contribute to reducing energy consumption while maintaining consistent comfort levels.
Together, these initiatives are helping 
us build a more responsive and efficient energy ecosystem. Early outcomes from pilot locations indicate tangible energy savings alongside improved temperature  consistency - demonstrating that operational efficiency and customer experience can go hand in hand. We are also collaborating with IITB-Monash to draw deeper insights into energy optimisation. Beyond measurable gains, these efforts are also improving equipment reliability and reducing manual intervention, reinforcing our commitment to smarter and more sustainable retail perations.
Expanding Renewable Energy
As part of our broader decarbonisation journey, we are steadily increasing our adoption of renewable energy across operations. Our distribution centres are an important starting point, where over one-third of electricity needs are already met through rooftop  solar installations.During FY26, we further expanded this footprint by implementing solar rooftop systems at an additional distribution centre, reinforcing our shift toward cleaner energy sources.
Looking ahead, we aim to scale 
renewable energy adoption across our network while continuing to enhance efficiency through smarter technologies. Together, these efforts reflect our commitment to building a more sustainable and resilient  energy future.
Packaging and Waste 
Management
As our operations grow, so does the 
responsibility to manage waste thoughtfully and efficiently. Across Trent’s value chain, most of the waste generated is non-hazardous - comprising materials such as plastics, cardboard cartons, fabric scraps, hangers, and metal fixtures from our logistics network, distribution centres, and retail stores. Smaller quantities of electronic waste are also generated through IT and operational equipment.
Over the past year, we have seen an 
increase in total plastic waste generation, in line with business growth. At the same time, plastic waste intensity per product has reduced, reflecting ongoing efforts to optimise material use and improve efficiency at scale.
To strengthen waste management 
practices, we continue to rely on a centralised system that enables segregation at source, traceability across the lifecycle, and compliant disposal through authorised partners. This structured approach ensures that waste is managed responsibly  while providing visibility into  improvement opportunities.

Alongside this, we are actively 
rethinking packaging and materials across our operations. Key initiatives include transitioning from single-use cardboard cartons to reusable logistics totes, adopting recycled hangers, and introducing compostable packaging materials and recycled metal fixtures. The shift to reusable totes, in particular, is helping streamline product movement across supply chain touchpoints - reducing packaging waste while also improving durability and handling efficiency.
Together, these efforts reflect a 
broader shift towards more circular practices, where reducing waste and improving resource efficiency  go hand in hand with  operational effectiveness.
Life Cycle Assessment  
(LCA)
As part of our ongoing efforts to strengthen data-driven sustainability practices, a Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) was undertaken for a 100% cotton product within the WES Casuals portfolio, manufactured in India. The assessment evaluates environmental impacts across key life cycle stages, including raw material sourcing, processing, and manufacturing, to identify material impact areas. Based on the current analysis, water consumption is estimated at ~2,289 litres per unit, with the majority attributable to cotton cultivation, consistent with industry-wide patterns. Additional estimated impacts include energy consumption (~7.01 MJ per unit), chemical use (~0.109 kg), wastewater generation (~1.68 litres), and solid waste (~0.044 kg). These findings, while subject to data assumptions and methodological boundaries typical of LCA studies, are being used to inform targeted interventions such as improved sourcing practices and  process efficiencies.
Building on this approach, the 
Company intends to expand LCA coverage to a broader set of products to deepen understanding of environmental hotspots across the portfolio. In parallel, efforts are being explored to introduce a Digital Product Passport, with the aim of enhancing product-level transparency, traceability, and data accessibility, in line with emerging global sustainability practices.
Extended Producer 
Responsibility (EPR)
Trent complies with Extended 
Producer Responsibility (EPR) regulations as a registered Brand Owner and Importer with the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB). Through certified recycling partners, plastic waste is collected and recycled into:
 Biodegradable bags
 Recycled cardboard
 Recycled paper  packaging materials
Water Stewardship
At Trent, water consumption within our operations remains primarily linked to everyday usage across stores, offices, and distribution centres. While our overall water footprint is relatively limited compared to  manufacturing-intensive sectors, we recognise the importance of managing this resource responsibly as we continue to grow.
Over the past year, total water 
consumption has increased in line with the expansion of our retail footprint and operational scale. At the same time, water intensity per product has seen a reduction, reflecting ongoing efforts to improve efficiency and optimise usage across locations.
These trends highlight a balanced 
approach - where growth is supported by conscious reductions in resource intensity. We continue to focus on driving responsible water practices, ensuring that even modest consumption is managed with care and efficiency.
Enabling Circular and 
Responsible Retail
We continue to move towards a more 
circular model - one that reduces resource use and extends product lifecycles. Across our operations, initiatives such as reusable logistics solutions and responsible sourcing practices are helping reduce environmental impact while improving efficiency. These steps, though incremental, collectively support our long-term vision of building a resilient, transparent, and environmentally responsible retail ecosystem.
Nature - Based Solutions  
We are advancing nature-based solutions through regenerative agriculture programme that supports sustainable cotton farming practices. Recognising the critical importance of water, we are also progressing a Sustainable Water Conservation and Security Initiative, aimed at promoting responsible water use and building long-term resilience within communities and ecosystems. Together, these efforts reflect our commitment to using resources thoughtfully while creating lasting value for both business and society.

Share Capital
Issuance of Bonus shares
With a view to rewarding the existing Shareholders and to 
enhance retail participation by improving affordability and 
liquidity of the Company’s equity shares, the Board of Directors 
(‘the Board’), at its meeting held on 22nd April 2026, approved 
the issue of bonus shares in the ratio of 1 (One) equity share 
of ` 1/- each for every 2 (Two) fully paid-up equity shares 
of ` 1/- each held by the Members of the Company as on  
4th June 2026, being the record date ﬁxed for determining 
the eligibility of Shareholders entitled to receive bonus shares 
(‘Bonus Issue’), subject to the approval of the Shareholders 
and other applicable statutory and regulatory approvals. 
The Bonus Issue will be effected by capitalising a sum not 
exceeding ` 17.78 Crore standing to the credit of the Securities 
Premium account as per the Audited Financial Statements for 
the ﬁnancial year ended 31st March 2026.
The bonus equity shares, once allotted, shall rank pari passu 
in all respects with the existing equity shares and shall be 
treated as an increase in the paid-up equity share capital of 
the Company.
Reclassi/f_ication of Authorized Share Capital
To simplify the authorized share capital structure and 
utilize the same for the proposed Bonus Issue and also 
to support any future capital raising requirements, the 
Board, at its meeting held on 22nd April 2026, approved 
the reclassiﬁcation of the Authorized Share Capital of the 
Company and consequent alteration of the Capital Clause of 
the Memorandum of Association. Accordingly, the Authorized 
Share Capital of the Company is proposed to be reclassiﬁed 
from:  ` 85,55,00,000/- (Rupees Eighty Five Crore Fifty Five 
Lakh Only) divided into multiple classes of shares, including 
equity shares, preference shares and other categories,  to 
` 85,55,00,000/- (Rupees Eighty Five Crore Fifty Five Lakh 
Only) divided into 85,55,00,000 equity shares of ` 1/- each, 
subject to the approval of the Shareholders.
Issuance of shares held under abeyance
The Board, at its meeting held on 22nd April 2026, approved 
the issue and allotment of 740 equity shares, which were held 
in abeyance pursuant to the rights issue undertaken by the 
Company in the year 2005, 2007 and 2010, to a Shareholder 
upon judicial clearance of his title to such shares. The said 
equity shares shall rank pari passu in all respects with the 
existing equity shares of the Company.Conseq uently, upon issuance of shares held in abeyance 
and the Bonus Issue, the revised paid-up equity share capital 
of the Company shall stand at ` 53,32,32,301/-, comprising 
53,32,32,301 equity shares of face value ` 1/- each.
Trent Limited - Employee Stock Option Plan 2026
The Board, at its meeting held on 22nd April 2026, approved 
the adoption of the ‘Trent Limited – Employee Stock Option 
Plan, 2026’ (‘ESOP 2026’ / ‘the Plan’), in accordance with 
the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 (‘the Act’) and 
the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Share Based 
Employee Beneﬁts and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021, as 
amended from time to time (‘SBEB Regulations’), subject 
to the approval of the Shareholders. The Plan is proposed 
to be implemented for the beneﬁt of eligible employees of 
the Company, including its subsidiary company(ies) and 
associate company(ies).
Under the Plan, the Company proposes to issue up to 
8,88,700 (Eight Lakh Eighty Eight Thousand Seven Hundred) 
equity shares, representing 0.25% of the issued equity share 
capital of the Company as on 31st March 2026, upon exercise 
of stock options granted to the eligible employees.
Dividend
The Board has recommended a Dividend of ` 6/- per equity 
share of ` 1/- each (600%) for the ﬁnancial year ended  
31st March 2026 (previous year: ` 5/- per Equity Share), 
subject to the approval of the Shareholders at the ensuing 
Annual General Meeting (‘AGM’). The total Dividend on equity 
shares for FY 2025-26, if approved by the Shareholders at 
the ensuing AGM, aggregating to ` 213.29 Crore, resulting 
in a Dividend pay-out of 11%. The said Dividend has been 
recommended in line with the Dividend Distribution Policy 
and will be paid out of the Proﬁts for the year.
In view of the proposed Bonus Issue, if approved by the 
Shareholders, the aforesaid Dividend per equity share, 
if declared, shall be proportionately reduced to reﬂect the 
increase in the number of equity shares, post Bonus Issue.
As per the provisions of the Income-Tax Act, 2025, Dividend 
paid or distributed by the Company shall be taxable in the 
hands of the Shareholders. Accordingly, the Company will 
pay the Dividend after deducting tax at source at applicable 
rates.Board’s Report

Performance Overview
Standalone Performance
During the year under review, the Company delivered 
a strong performance, driven by robust traction 
across its brands and continued store expansion. The 
Company now operates a signiﬁcant portfolio of more 
than 1,250 “large-box” fashion stores, with presence 
across 321 cities (including 3 cities in the UAE). In  
FY 2025-26, the Company opened 60 Westside and 212 
Zudio stores (including 4 stores in the UAE) and consolidated 
8 Westside and 14 Zudio stores. As of 31st March 2026, the store portfolio included 300 Westside, 963 Zudio 
(including 6 stores in the UAE) and 23 stores across other 
lifestyle concepts and a total footprint of over 17.7 million  
sq. ft. across fashion brands.
Consistent focus on merchandise, price architecture, supply 
chain and disciplined execution, enabled the Company to 
deliver consistent proﬁtable growth.
Revenue from Operations for FY 2025-26 stood at  
`  19,701.41 Crore as against `  16,668.11 Crore in  
FY 2024-25 registering a growth of 18.20%. Proﬁt After Tax is  
`  1,967.82 Crore in FY 2025-26 in comparison to  
` 1,584.84 Crore in the previous year. Total Comprehensive 
Income is ` 1,966.14 Crore in FY 2025-26 vs ` 1,580.97 Crore in 
FY 2024-25. Proﬁt After Tax and Total Comprehensive Income 
for FY 2025-26 included an Exceptional Loss of ` 25.79 Crore 
on account of the charge related to the implementation of the 
new Labour Codes effective from 21st November 2025. The 
Company will assess any further impact upon notiﬁcation of 
the applicable Central and State Rules.
Consolidated Performance
At the consolidated level, the Company achieved strong 
growth and proﬁtability, driven by steady performance across 
its businesses.
Total Consolidated Revenue from Operations  for FY 2025–26  
stood at ` 20,074.21 Crore as against ` 17,134.61 Crore in  
FY 2024-25, registering a growth of 17.16%. Consolidated 
Proﬁt After Tax for FY 2025-26 is ` 1,721.33 Crore vs  
` 1,534.41 Crore in FY 2024-25. The Proﬁt After Tax for  
FY 2025-26 included an Exceptional Loss of ` 26.11 Crore 
on account of the implementation of the new Labour Codes 
effective from 21st November 2025. The Company will assess 
any further impact upon notiﬁcation of the applicable Central and 
State Rules.

 Directors’ Responsibility Statement
Based on the framework of internal ﬁnancial controls and 
compliance systems established and maintained by the 
Company, the work performed by the Internal, Statutory 
and Secretarial Auditors and external consultants, including 
audit of internal ﬁnancial controls over ﬁnancial reporting 
by the Statutory Auditors and the reviews performed by 
management and the relevant Board Committees, including 
the Audit Committee, the Board is of the opinion that the 
Company’s internal ﬁnancial controls were adequate and 
effective during the ﬁnancial year ended 31st March 2026.
Accordingly, pursuant to Section 134(3)(c) and 134(5) of the 
Act, the Board of Directors, to the best of their information 
and knowledge, conﬁrm that:
•  in the preparation of the Annual Accounts for the 
ﬁnancial year ended 31st March 2026, the applicable 
accounting standards have been followed and there is 
no material departure from the same;
•  they have selected such accounting policies and 
applied them consistently and made judgments and 
estimates that are reasonable and prudent so as to give 
a true and fair view of the state of affairs of the Company 
at the end of the ﬁnancial year and of the Proﬁt of the 
Company for that period;
•  they have taken proper and sufﬁcient care for the 
maintenance of adequate accounting records 
in accordance with the provisions of the Act for 
safeguarding the assets of the Company and for 
preventing and detecting fraud and other irregularities;
•  they have prepared the Annual Accounts on a going 
concern basis;
•  they have laid down internal ﬁnancial controls to be 
followed by the Company and that such internal ﬁnancial 
controls are adequate and operating effectively; and
•  they have devised proper systems to ensure compliance 
with the provisions of all applicable laws and that such 
systems are adequate and operating effectively.

Declaration of Independence
In terms of Section 149 of the Act and the SEBI Listing 
Regulations, Mr. Jayesh Merchant, Mr. Ravneet Singh Gill, 
Ms. Hema Ravichandar and Ms. Kiran Mazumdar Shaw are 
the Independent Directors of the Company as on the date of 
this Report.
In terms of the SEBI Listing Regulations, the Independent 
Directors have conﬁrmed that they are not aware of any 
circumstance or situation, which exists or may be reasonably 
anticipated, that could impair or impact their ability to 
discharge their duties with an objective independent 
judgement and without any external inﬂuence. Based upon 
the declarations received from the Independent Directors, the 
Board of Directors has conﬁrmed that they meet the criteria of 
independence as mentioned under Section 149(6) of the Act 
and Regulation 16(1)(b) of the SEBI Listing Regulations and 
that they are independent of the management.
In the opinion of the Board, there has been no change in the 
circumstances affecting their status as Independent Directors 
of the Company and the Board is satisﬁed of the integrity, 
expertise and experience (including proﬁciency in terms of 
Section 150(1) of the Act and applicable rules thereunder) of

aligned with the Guidance Note on Board Evaluation issued 
by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).
Evaluation of Directors
The performance evaluation of Individual Directors, inter alia , 
includes assessment of their knowledge and competence, 
fulﬁlment of ﬁduciary and statutory duties, ability to function 
as an effective team Member, initiative and engagement, 
availability and attendance at meetings, commitment, 
integrity and independence. It also covers their contribution 
and participation in Board and Committee meetings, as 
well as guidance and support provided to the management 
outside such meetings. In addition, the Chairman is evaluated 
on speciﬁc aspects of his role, including effectiveness of 
leadership, ability to steer meetings constructively and 
impartially, consideration of Shareholders’ interests, and 
the ability to mentor, motivate and provide guidance to the 
Executive Directors.Evaluation of Board
The Board evaluation includes, inter alia , assessment of the 
Board’s composition and structure, effectiveness of meetings 
and overall functioning, discharge of key responsibilities, 
delegation of authority to Committees, effectiveness of Board 
processes, adequacy and timeliness of information, and the 
quality of interaction and relationship between the Board and 
the management.
Evaluation of Board Committees
The evaluation of Committees encompasses, inter alia , their 
mandate and composition, effectiveness in discharging 
assigned responsibilities, structure and frequency of 
meetings, independence from the Board, contribution to 
Board decision-making, and the quality of interaction with the 
Board and the management.
Evaluation Process
During FY 2025-26, the Board carried out an evaluation of its 
own performance, the performance of its committees and that 
of Individual Directors. The evaluation was conducted through 
an online self-assessment mechanism. The Chairperson of 
the NRC held detailed discussions with Individual Directors to 
seek their inputs on the effectiveness of the Board, Committee 
functioning, and governance processes. A comprehensive 
presentation on Board effectiveness was placed before the 
Board at its meeting held on 26th March 2026.
The performance evaluation of Independent Directors was 
undertaken by the entire Board, excluding the Independent 
Director being evaluated. Further, a separate meeting of 
the Independent Directors was held on 26th March 2026, 
wherein the performance of the Board and Non-Independent 
Directors (including the Chairman) was discussed taking 
into consideration feedback received from all Directors. The 
Independent Directors provided their collective feedback to 
the Board, the Chairman and the Managing Director.
The Board effectiveness evaluation process facilitates 
periodic assessment of the Board’s functioning and 
governance practices, promoting continuous enhancement 
and ensuring alignment with the Company’s evolving 
strategic priorities.Board’s Report

 Vigil Mechanism / Whistle Blower Policy
The Company believes in the conduct of the affairs of its 
constituents in a fair and transparent manner by adopting 
the highest standards of professionalism, honesty, integrity 
and ethical behavior. In line with the Tata Code of Conduct 
(‘TCoC’), any actual or potential violation, howsoever 
insigniﬁcant or perceived as such, are treated as a matter of 
serious concern for the Company. The role of the employees 
in pointing out such violations of the TCoC is given utmost 
importance.
The Company has in place a Whistle Blower Policy in 
compliance with the provisions of the Act and the SEBI Listing 
Regulations. The said Policy is available on the Company’s 
website at https://docs.trent-tata.com/Whistlebl ower_Policy.
pdf
The Whistle Blower Policy encourages Directors, employees 
and other stakeholders to promptly report any actual or 
possible violation of the TCoC or any event that he or she 
becomes aware of that could affect the business or reputation 
of the Company. All the stakeholders have various channels to 
voice their concerns and are encouraged to report the same 
internally for resolution. The Company ensures protection 
for the Whistle Blowers and any attempts to intimidate the 
Whistle Blower would be treated as a violation of the TCoC 
and subject to appropriate action. The Managing Director, the 
Chief Human Resources Ofﬁcer, the Chief Financial Ofﬁcer 
and the Chief Ethics Ofﬁcer meet regularly and provide 
oversight to ethics related governance. All incidents that are 
reported are investigated and suitable action is taken in line 
with the Whistle Blower Policy.
A report indicating the number of cases reported, 
investigations conducted including the status update is 
presented before the Audit Committee, on a quarterly basis. 
The Chairperson of the NRC remains present during these 
discussions.

 Risk Management
The Company has adopted a comprehensive Enterprise 
Risk Management (‘ERM’) structure prescribed under the 
Committee of Sponsoring Organization of the Treadway 
Commission (‘COSO’), 2017 framework. The ERM framework 
has also been integrated with the Company’s strategy 
planning and business performance review processes.
The aforesaid framework covers business, ﬁnancial, 
operational, HR, reputational, sectoral, cybersecurity, ESG 
and any other risks determined by the Risk Management 
Committee (‘RMC’). The strategic risks forming part of the 
ERM process are also aligned with the audit universe, to the 
extent seen appropriate / relevant.
The Risk Management Policy has been adopted by the Board 
and is consistent with the provisions of the Act and the SEBI 
Listing Regulations.
The Company has laid down governance procedures around 
information, communication and risk reporting to the RMC, 
Audit Committee and the Board of Directors about risk 
assessment, mitigation, effectiveness, evaluation and related 
outcome and status.
A central risk management team under the leadership 
of the Chief Financial Ofﬁcer facilitates execution of the 
risk management practices in the Company, in the areas 
of risk identiﬁcation, assessment, monitoring, mitigation 
and reporting. The RMC oversees the Company’s risk 
management processes and controls.
The Company periodically reviews and improves the 
adequacy and effectiveness of its risk management process 
considering the rapidly changing business environment and 
evolving complexities.

 Health and Safety
Health and Safety Management System
The Company remains committed to providing a safe and 
healthy work environment across its ofﬁces, retail stores, 
and distribution centres. Its Health and Safety (‘H&S’) Polic y 
is aligned with the Tata Group Retail Safety Standards and 
the Tata Health and Safety Management System (‘THSMS’) 
and complies with the applicable regulations. The Policy 
also applies to contractors and third-party service providers 
operating at the Company’s sites.
To promote a culture of safety, the Company conducts 
regular internal and external safety audits. Internal audits 
are carried out quarterly by senior leadership teams, while 
external auditors conduct electrical safety audits across 
facilities. Audit ﬁndings are recorded in a centralized system, 
and corrective actions are implemented promptly to ensure 
timely closure.
The Company’s key governance mechanism includes monthly 
Safety Committee meetings Chaired by the Managing Director, 
where safety performance, audit closures, and improvement 
initiatives are discussed and reviewed. The Company also 
participates in the periodic assessments under the Tata 
Safety Excellence Model, conducted by the Tata Business 
Excellence Group, to evaluate the effectiveness and maturity 
of its safety management systems.
Hazard Identi/f_ication, Risk Assessment and Incident 
Investigation
Workplace safety is a key priority for the Company and is 
closely overseen at the highest levels of the organization.  The H&S Manual provides a structured framework based on 
the Tata Group Retail Safety Standards, outlining the practices 
required to maintain a safe and healthy work environment.
The Company has instituted a robust H&S Management 
System, which enables proactive identiﬁcation and 
mitigation of risks through the Hazard Identiﬁcation and Risk 
Assessment (‘HIRA’) methodology. A cross-functional team 
comprising safety ofﬁcers, maintenance personnel, and 
trained volunteers undertakes HIRA assessments across 
all locations. The team undergoes periodic training, both 
internal and external, in line with the requirements prescribed 
by the Tata Group’s centralized safety team.
HIRA assessments are conducted periodically, enabling 
the Company to identify, evaluate, and effectively mitigate 
potential risks. Incident investigations are carried out w ith 
diligence to ensure root causes are addressed and learnings 
are integrated  into future safety practices.
 Policy on Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal of 
Sexual Harassment at Workplace
The Company has zero tolerance for sexual harassment 
at workplace and has adopted a gender-neutral Policy on 
Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal of Sexual Harassment 
at the Workplace, with the objective of providing a safe and 
secure working environment for all employees. The Company 
has in place duly constituted Internal Complaints Committee 
(‘ICC’) in accordance with the Sexual Harassment of Women 
at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 
2013 (‘POSH Act’).
The Company conducts periodic sensitization sessions for 
employees across the organization to build awareness of the 
POSH Policy and the provisions of the POSH Act. During the 
year under review, the ICC received 17 complaints, of which 
3 were pending as of 31st March 2026. Out of the pending 
complaints 1 was resolved subsequently and 2 were under 
investigation with the ICC and were within the 90 days 
timeframe. N o complaints remained pending beyond 90 days.

(A) Conservation of Energy
  During FY 2025-26, the Company continued to 
strengthen its focus on energy conservation by 
scaling energy-efﬁcient solutions across its operations 
and reducing overall energy intensity. Leveraging 
technology-enabled interventions, the Company 
expanded the deployment of smart Internet of Things 
(IoT) systems to centrally monitor and control lighting 
and air-conditioning parameters, enabling optimized 
energy usage across a store network of over 700 stores. 
The Company incurred an expenditure of approximately 
` 6.6 Crore during the year towards these energy 
conservation initiatives.
  Further, the Company continued deploying energy-
efﬁcient inverter air conditioners across all stores, 
supporting improved cooling performance while 
optimising power consumption. Further, store and ofﬁce 
infrastructure was enhanced through the increased 
use of high-lumen LED lighting, high-reﬂector facades, 
improved air circulation through the use of fans, and 
application of ﬁlms on glass surfaces, contributing to 
reduced electricity consumption and improved energy 
performance. The Company has increased the share of 
renewable energy by installing rooftop solar panels and 
sourcing green power. Rooftop solar installations meet 
over one-third of electricity demand at three distribution 
centres.

to secure, scalable cloud platforms. This 
ensures better uptime, disaster recovery, and 
lower infrastructure management overhead. 
Moving to the cloud has also enabled 
faster deployments, improved security, 
and seamless integration across business 
applications.
  •  RFID technology deployment across stores 
and distribution centers: The Company 
expanded use of RFID (Radio Frequency 
Identiﬁcation) across retail stores and 
distribution centers (DCs). This has led 
to signiﬁcant improvements in inventory 
accuracy, reduced cycle count times, and 
faster inward and outward processing at DCs. 
The ability to identify SKUs at a granular level, 
in real time, has not only improved operational 
efﬁciency but also enhanced ability to 
replenish stores with the right products at the 
right time.
  •  Adoption of Product Lifecycle Management 
(‘PLM’) System: A modern PLM platform was 
adopted by the Company to streamline the 
design-to-market process across the apparel 
and fashion categories. The platform facilitates 
digital collaboration between design, buying, 
and sourcing teams, reducing lead times and 
improving accuracy in product speciﬁcations. 
It also ensures traceability, compliance, and 
consistent quality across product categories 
and supplier networks.
  •  Implementation of a Transport Management 
System (‘TMS’): The Company has 
implemented a TMS to bring more visibility 
and control over logistics operations. The TMS 
enables route optimization, real-time shipment

General Economic Backdrop and Industry Outlook
India’s economic 
ascent over the past three decades marks a journey of successive reforms, technological advancements, beneﬁts of dynamic demographics and political stability. India continues to outperform major global economies, with GDP growth reported at 7.6% in FY 2025-26, as per the Second Advance Estimates by National Statistical Oﬃce (NSO) and remains on track to become the world’s third-largest economy by 2030. Private consumption remains a key driver of this momentum, led by discretionary and services spending. The macroeconomic environment 
in FY 2025-26 remained complex, shaped by trade challenges due to higher tariffs and general trade protectionism and geopolitical tensions in West Asia. Despite this, the Indian economy remains fundamentally resilient, and its long-term economic promise remains intact. Structural domestic drivers, a young population, rapid urbanisation, and deep digital penetration, continue to underpin a dynamic and expanding consumption base. 
Consumer aspirations are increasingly 
aligned with global trends, particularly in fashion, lifestyle, and food. Also, the Indian market is heterogenous and geographically diverse. For instance, Southern India has been materially ahead in per capita income/ consumption levels. This diversity coupled with waves of evolution playing out, is both a challenge to navigate and an opportunity  to leverage.
Retail Sector
India is the world’s fourth-largest retail market. Valued at ~ ` 90-95 Lakh 
Crores (~$ 1 Tn) in CY 2025
1, the 
market is projected to reach  ~` 210 -215 Lakh Crores ($ 2.3 Tn) 
by CY 2035
1, driven by rising

preference for branded products and the expansion of modern retail infrastructure including malls, mixed-use developments and airport retail hubs. These developments collectively position the organised retail industry for sustained growth.

Market t
India’s fashion and lifestyle sector is 
undergoing a transformative phase, propelled by digitalisation, evolving consumer preferences, and increased global access and exposure. The market, valued at ~ ` 12 Lakh Crores*
